content.title: 2026 NBA playoffs: Full schedule, how to watch live, format, teams, key players, and biggest storylines
content.text: The 2026 NBA postseason has started, and the race for the Larry O’Brien Trophy is taking shape. Here is everything to know, from the schedule and format to the stars, contenders and first-round storylines to follow.Picture by Kenneth Richmond/Getty ImagesBy Will ImboUpdated on 18 April 2026 06:46 GMT+07 min readThe playoff bracket is not complete yet, but the 2026 NBA postseason has already burst into life. With the Play-In Tournament having begun on 14 April and the first round of the playoffs set to tip off on Saturday 18 April, attention is already turning from qualification to survival. Oklahoma City enter as defending champions, Detroit lead the East after a standout regular season, and a field packed with proven stars, rising contenders, and dangerous lower seeds promises plenty of intrigue from the opening weekend. From the full schedule and confirmed matchups to the key players, storylines, and how to watch live, here are the main things you need to know about the 2026 NBA playoffs.FRA v USA - Men's Gold Medal Game | Basketball | Olympic Games Paris 2024The Men's Basketball Gold Medal Game took place on 10/08/2024 at Bercy Arena, Paris. For the fifth time in a row, United States of America claimed the Gold with an 98:87 win against France.How do the NBA playoffs work? The NBA playoffs are a four-round, best-of-seven postseason tournament that decides the champion of the North American elite men's basketball league. Once the Play-In Tournament concludes — determining the seventh and eighth seeds in both the Eastern and Western conferences — the 16-team playoff bracket is set. Each series is determined by seeding, with the No. 1 seed facing the No. 8 seed, No. 2 playing No. 7, and so on. The higher seed gets home-court advantage, hosting games 1, 2, 5, and game 7 if it's needed, while the lower seed hosts games 3, 4, and 6. The first team to win four games moves on to the next round. The opening round is followed by the conference semi-finals, conference finals and, ultimately, the NBA Finals, where the Eastern and Western Conference champions meet for the Larry O’Brien Trophy.Key players and storylines to follow Can the Thunder be the first repeat champions in eight years? The Thunder won the franchise’s first NBA title since relocating from Seattle to Oklahoma City last year, beating the Indiana Pacers in a seven-game Finals that went right down to the wire. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was central to that run — and to the Thunder’s entire 2024-25 campaign — becoming just the fourth player to win the MVP award, the scoring title, and Finals MVP in the same season. The Canadian did not retain the scoring crown this year, with Luka Dončić leading the league on 33.5 points per game, but Gilgeous-Alexander still finished second on 31.1. Oklahoma City were not quite the same juggernaut as a year ago, but they still ranked first in defensive rating and seventh in offensive rating, and remain a leading contender to become the first team to repeat as champions since the Golden State Warriors in 2017 and 2018. Can Victor Wembanyama fast-track the Spurs into title contention? San Antonio’s rise has been one of the stories of the season. The Spurs went 62-20 after missing the playoffs a year ago, becoming just the fourth team in NBA history to win at least 60 games the season after failing to qualify. Wembanyama averaged 25.0 points per game, led the league with 197 blocks, and became only the third player to lead the NBA in blocks per game in three straight seasons. The question now is whether a young Spurs team can keep that edge when the postseason slows into more half-court basketball.Picture by Joshua Gateley/Getty ImagesGilgeous-Alexander (#2) and the Thunder struggled against Wembanyama and the Spurs this season, going 1-4 in their head-to-head contests.Can Detroit turn its remarkable rise into a deep run? Two seasons after a 14-win campaign, Detroit finished 60-22 and claimed the East’s top seed behind the league’s No. 2 defense. Cade Cunningham averaged 24.2 points per game and returned late in the season from a collapsed lung, but the Pistons also showed their depth by posting a strong net rating even during his absence. They became just the third team in the past 15 seasons to lead the NBA in both steals and blocks, which helps explain why they already look far more than a feel-good story. Can Boston’s “gap year” become something bigger? Boston still look every bit like a contender. The Celtics finished 56-26 with the league’s second-ranked offence and fourth-ranked defence, while Jaylen Brown led them in scoring at 28.7 points per game. The bigger swing factor, though, is Jayson Tatum: his return less than a year after an Achilles tear has already been remarkable, but if he can get close to his previous level — and if Boston’s thin centre rotation holds up — the Celtics have the balance to make another serious run. What other storylines could shape the playoffs? LeBron James will tie John Stockton and Karl Malone for the most playoff appearances in NBA history with 19, and the Lakers may need every bit of that experience in a difficult first-round series against Houston following injuries to Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves. Denver remain a major threat on the other side of the West, with Nikola Jokić leading the league in rebounds and assists per game — the first player to do that in a season since 1969-70 — while the Nuggets also finished with the NBA’s top offence.Picture by Ronald Martinez/Getty ImagesCunningham (#2) is chasing his first NBA Finals appearance; James, his 11th.What is the schedule for the 2026 NBA playoffs? The 2026 SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament runs from 14 to 17 April, before the first round of the NBA playoffs begins on 18 April. All times are Eastern Time Zone. 2026 NBA Play-In Tournament schedule Tuesday, 14 April Heat (10) 126-127 Hornets (9) Trail Blazers (8) 114-110 vs Suns (7) Wednesday, 15 April Magic (8) 97-109 76ers (7) Warriors (10) 126-121 Clippers (9) Friday, 17 April Magic (8) 121-90 Hornets (9) Suns (7) 111-96 Warriors (10) What is the NBA playoff matchup schedule for Game 1s? Saturday, 18 April 2026 (5) Toronto Raptors at (4) Cleveland Cavaliers — 1 p.m. (6) Minnesota Timberwolves at (3) Denver Nuggets — 3:30 p.m. (6) Atlanta Hawks at (3) New York Knicks — 6 p.m. (5) Houston Rockets at (4) Los Angeles Lakers — 8:30 p.m. Sunday, 19 April 2026 (7) Philadelphia 76ers at (2) Boston Celtics — 1 p.m. (8) Phoenix Suns at (1) Oklahoma City Thunder — 3:30 p.m. (8) Orlando Magic at (1) Detroit Pistons — 6:30 p.m. (7) Portland Trail Blazers at (2) San Antonio Spurs — 9 p.m. 2026 NBA playoffs key dates 14-17 April: SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament 18 April: First round of the NBA playoffs begins 4 May: Conference semi-finals begin (possible move-up to 2-3 May) 19 May: Eastern Conference finals begin (possible move-up to 17 May) 20 May: Western Conference finals begin (possible move-up to 18 May) 3 June: NBA Finals 2026 Game 1 5 June: NBA Finals 2026 Game 2 8 June: NBA Finals 2026 Game 3 10 June: NBA Finals 2026 Game 4 13 June: NBA Finals 2026 Game 5 (if necessary) 16 June: NBA Finals 2026 Game 6 (if necessary) 19 June: NBA Finals 2026 Game 7 (if necessary) How to watch the NBA playoffs Viewers in the U.S. will be able to watch the 2026 NBA playoffs on ABC/ESPN, NBC/Peacock, and Amazon Prime Video. During the first round and conference semi-finals, games will be split across those broadcast partners, with the Eastern Conference finals set for ESPN/ABC, the Western Conference finals for NBC/Peacock, and the NBA Finals on ABC. The SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament is exclusive to Prime Video.
